industries: Banking and fintech, continental-scale manufacturing and regional corporate headquarters anchor Latin America's largest market.
intro:
São Paulo concentrates Latin America's project firepower: Faria Lima's banks and Nubank-led fintechs iterate at Silicon Valley pace, the industrial belt runs the continent's largest manufacturing programs, and global firms manage their South American portfolios from Paulista towers. Brazil's PMI chapters are among the world's largest, so PMP recognition is deep; the tech scene has made Scrum credentials equally mainstream. Live online training runs continuously through the year for São Paulo, with weekend Saturday–Sunday and weekday Wednesday–Thursday cohorts timed to sensible local hours; the schedule below shows the exact São Paulo start and finish for each upcoming batch. The package is constant: live weekend instruction in English, exam application support, calibrated mock exams, and trainer access until you certify. Brazilian learners train in English, which doubles as preparation for the multinational delivery roles most target.

São Paulo concentrates Latin America's corporate delivery: the banks and fintechs of Faria Lima run continuous regulatory and product change, industrial groups manage capital programs across the interior from headquarters here, and global capability centres add international delivery demand. Certification legible across borders matters in a market this connected to global capital. Training is live online across two consecutive days shown in São Paulo local time on this page, delivered in English — the working language of the international programs that pay the premium. The sourced São Paulo entries in the salary table below give dated, named local figures. The employer list shows the finance-industrial-GCC mix hiring certified professionals, and institutions can certify change teams at scale through private cohorts.
